keyChanges.title: Jefferies cuts Tesla EBIT forecast 37%, lowers PT to $350 — August 7 post-earnings follow-through
keyChanges.description: Jefferies analyst Philippe Houchois cut his Tesla price target to $350 from $400 on August 7, while maintaining a Hold rating. The primary driver was a 37% reduction in the firm's 2026 EBIT forecast to $3.9 billion, citing weaker-than-expected operating leverage from Q2 results. This is a material post-earnings follow-through note — not merely a reaction-day adjustment — arriving two weeks after the July 22 print and reinforcing that the Q2 earnings miss is being re-underwritten into forward model revisions, not treated as a one-quarter anomaly. Jefferies is notable because it had previously maintained a more neutral-to-constructive stance; this cut signals broader institutional consensus anchoring. The full-year 2026 non-GAAP EPS consensus now sits at approximately $2.08 per Tesla's own July 17 compiled consensus, but with EBIT estimates being revised down across desks, the gap between guidance and reality is widening.

sentiment.headline: negative
sentiment.rationale: A 37% forward EBIT cut from a major sell-side house two weeks post-earnings is not a margin-of-error revision — it signals that Q2 operational underperformance is being structurally embedded in consensus. The Hold rating at $350 implies the stock is still overvalued at current levels.

positive_signals: Jefferies maintained Hold (not downgraded to Sell), suggesting no catastrophic deterioration thesis
Tesla's Q2 revenue beat ($28.24B vs $25.71B consensus) preserved top-line credibility
negative_signals: 37% EBIT forecast cut to $3.9B — one of the deepest single-desk revisions post-Q2

No major bank issued an upward PT revision in the August 6-15 window
Analyst consensus (47-analyst S&P Global poll) average PT at $396.62 — still above stock but trending toward $350 floor

key_metrics.target: Prior Jefferies PT $400; market needed op margin recovery toward 5%+
key_metrics.trajectory: Sell-side anchoring lower; PT corridor $350-$400 now institutional consensus midpoint

keyChanges.title: TSLA bounces from $297 low to ~$330-345 — sentiment recovery without fundamental repair
keyChanges.description: Tesla stock rebounded from a 52-week intraday low of $297.38 (hit in late July) to approximately $330-345 by the August 6-15 window, a ~14-16% technical bounce. As of August 14, TSLA was trading around $313-$345 depending on session. The recovery is driven by sentiment factors: a proposed multi-billion-dollar solar manufacturing facility (Project Crystal Sun) in Texas, news of a UAW/labor strike ending at a Midwestern supplier, and positive framing of July China wholesale figures (93,579 units, Tesla China's best month of 2026). However, analysis published August 15 (247 Wall St.) specifically identifies the bounce as sentiment-driven while labeling three structural problems as unresolved: (1) operating margin must recover toward double digits without regulatory credits; (2) free cash flow must return to positive while $25B+ capex continues; (3) governance requires an independent chair or credible capital allocation framework. The stock is down approximately 23.8% YTD and 13.5% over one month, making any bounce a relief rally against a sharply negative trend.

sentiment.headline: neutral
sentiment.rationale: Headlines frame the bounce as 'recovery.' Reality is the stock remains -24% YTD, the P/E is ~306x, operating margin is 1.4%, FCF is negative $1.09B, and the three structural problems cited (margin, FCF, governance) have not changed. A bounce from an oversold extreme is not a fundamental inflection.

keyChanges.title: Tesla China: domestic sales fell 9% YoY H1 2026 while exports surge 127% — headline wholesale figures mask domestic collapse
keyChanges.description: Data published in the August 4 window (Electrek, CnEVPost, Drive Tesla Canada) reveals a critical distinction in Tesla's China performance that is being obscured by headline wholesale numbers. Giga Shanghai's July 2026 wholesale total of 93,579 units was Tesla China's strongest month of 2026 and up 38% YoY — but this headline number bundles exports. Domestic China deliveries in July were only 27,249 units, down approximately 33% from July 2025. Over H1 2026, domestic retail sales in China came in at 238,955 vehicles, down 9% YoY and 19% below Tesla's H1 2023 peak of 294,105. Exports out of Giga Shanghai surged 127% to 228,994 units in H1. For Q2 specifically, exports (128,394) edged past domestic China deliveries (126,157) for the first time ever. This is a structural deterioration story: Tesla is losing China domestic market share to BYD, Xiaomi, NIO, and others while compensating by flooding European, Canadian, and Asian markets from Giga Shanghai. The domestic China volume base supporting the Q2 global delivery beat is thus smaller and more vulnerable than aggregate wholesale data suggests.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: Headlines report 'Tesla China wholesale surges 38%' and 'Tesla China's best month of 2026.' Reality is domestic Chinese deliveries fell 33% in July and 9% in H1. The wholesale surge is entirely export-driven. Giga Shanghai is being repositioned as a global export hub to compensate for domestic market share loss — a defensive restructuring, not demand strength.

Exports surging 127% H1 YoY shows Giga Shanghai is operationally competitive as a global production hub

key_metrics.trajectory: Domestic market share loss accelerating; export volumes masking the decline in headline numbers

keyChanges.title: Q3 2026 delivery consensus forming around 461,500 — GLJ Research sees miss at 456,600; buy-side whisper above 470,000
keyChanges.description: With Q3 2026 ending September 30, early-window sell-side estimates are forming around a consensus of approximately 461,500 deliveries per GLJ Research's August tracking. GLJ Research (Gordon Johnson, Sell) updated its own Q3 estimate upward to 456,600 from 449,000 based on China data and European daily sales reporting, while still projecting a miss vs. the 461,500 consensus. The buy-side whisper number is reportedly above 470,000. This sets up a tight beat-or-miss dynamic heading into Q3 reporting. Context: Q2 delivered 480,126 (well above consensus 406,024) partly on inventory drawdown (production was 28,000 units below deliveries). A normalized Q3 without that inventory tailwind would likely print lower than Q2. Full-year 2026 consensus remains around 1.65-1.73M deliveries across various polling sources, compared to management's 20-30% growth guidance (~1.9-2.0M), a gap of ~250,000-350,000 units that management has not addressed since the Q2 call.

sentiment.headline: neutral
sentiment.rationale: The consensus estimate of ~461,500 would represent a quarter-over-quarter decline from Q2's 480,126. A 'beat' scenario at 470k+ still implies a QoQ delivery decline. Musk's full-year 20-30% growth guidance requires ~1.9-2.0M total, leaving an H2 run-rate that looks increasingly unreachable without major volume catalyst (Model Y L, Cybercab). GLJ maintains Sell at $24.86 — a stark contrast to the $422 consensus PT.

positive_signals: GLJ raised its own Q3 estimate to 456,600 (up from 449,000) on improving China data
Buy-side whisper >470,000 — institutional bulls expect another beat-vs-consensus

negative_signals: Q3 consensus ~461,500 implies QoQ decline from Q2's 480,126

No Q3 IR-published delivery consensus has been released by Tesla as of August 15
China domestic demand remains structurally weak (9% YoY decline H1)

key_metrics.target: Musk guidance: 20-30% growth (~1.9-2.0M FY2026); Buy-side whisper >470k Q3
key_metrics.trajectory: Full-year guidance gap ~250-350k units; Q3 delivery likely to be QoQ decline regardless of beat/miss vs. consensus
